stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave is mainly used to communicate with artificial satellites?

options.content: Microwaves
options.rationale: Correct: they pass through the atmosphere.

options.content: Gamma rays
Ultraviolet
X-rays

explanation: Communication with satellites is mainly by microwaves, which pass straight through the atmosphere.

stem: Why can a satellite TV dish on a house stay pointed in one fixed direction?

options.content: The satellite is geostationary: it stays above the same point on the Earth.
The satellite does not move at all.
options.rationale: It orbits, but in step with the Earth's rotation.

options.content: The Earth does not rotate.
options.rationale: The Earth rotates once a day.

options.content: The signal fills the whole sky equally.
options.rationale: The dish must point at the satellite.

explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits above the equator once every 24 hours, so it stays above the same point and the dish can be fixed.

stem: A geostationary satellite orbits the Earth above the equator once every 24 hours.
explanation: That is why it stays above the same point on the Earth's surface.

stem: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used by Bluetooth?

options.content: Gamma rays
Ultraviolet
Radio waves
options.rationale: Correct: they pass through walls and are weakened, giving a short range.

options.content: X-rays

explanation: Bluetooth uses low-power radio waves, which pass through walls but are weakened in doing so.

stem: Why are microwaves used for mobile phones and wireless internet?

options.content: They are completely absorbed by buildings.
options.rationale: Then signals would not reach indoors.

options.content: They can pass through some walls and need only a short aerial.
They are ionising.
They travel faster than other EM waves.
options.rationale: All EM waves travel at the same speed.

explanation: Microwaves penetrate some walls and only need short aerials for transmitting and receiving.

stem: Why are optical fibres used for high-speed broadband?

options.content: The fibres carry an electric current.
Glass is transparent to visible light and some infrared, which can carry data at very high rates.
Light in glass travels faster than in a vacuum.
The light leaks out to nearby homes.
options.rationale: Total internal reflection keeps it inside.

explanation: Visible light and short-wavelength infrared pass along glass with little loss and carry very high data rates.

options.content: A signal that varies continuously
A signal that can only be sent by radio
options.rationale: Digital signals can travel by fibre, cable or radio.

options.content: A signal that cannot carry sound
A signal with only a few values, usually two (1 and 0)

explanation: A digital signal takes only a few values, usually two: on and off, 1 and 0.

stem: Sound can be transmitted either as an analogue signal or as a digital signal.
explanation: A microphone gives an analogue signal; it can be sampled and converted to a digital signal for transmission.

stem: Why can a digital signal travel a long distance with very little loss of quality?

options.content: Digital signals do not pick up noise.
options.rationale: They do; the noise can be removed.

options.content: Digital signals travel faster than analogue signals.
Digital signals do not get weaker as they travel.
Regenerators recognise each pulse as 1 or 0 and send out a clean copy, removing the noise.

explanation: Each regenerator rebuilds a perfect digital signal, so noise does not build up as it does when analogue signals are amplified.
hints: What happens to noise when an analogue signal is amplified?

stem: Select **all** the benefits of digital signalling.

options.content: The signal can travel further, because it can be regenerated accurately.
The signal travels faster than light.
No aerial is ever needed.
options.rationale: Not a benefit of digital signals.

options.content: The signal never gets weaker.
Noise can be removed when the signal is regenerated.
Data can be sent at a higher rate.

explanation: Digital signals allow faster data transmission and a longer range, because regenerators remove the noise.
hints: Think about data rate and what regenerators can do.

stem: Match each use with the electromagnetic waves it uses.
explanation: Mobile phones: microwaves. Bluetooth: radio waves. Optical fibres: visible light or infrared.

stem: A rural school connects to the internet by a satellite link and shares the connection by Wi-Fi.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the type of electromagnetic wave used to communicate with the satellite.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Data are sent as digital signals. Explain one advantage of digital over analogue signals.

points.description: Noise can be removed when the signal is regenerated (it is only recognised as 1 or 0)
so the signal can travel further / data can be sent at a higher rate without loss of quality

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Some satellite phone networks use low-orbit satellites. What is an advantage of a low orbit compared with a geostationary orbit?

options.content: The satellite stays above the same point on the Earth.
Fewer satellites are needed to cover the Earth.
options.rationale: More are needed, because each moves across the sky.

options.content: The signals travel a shorter distance, so there is less delay.
The signals can be sent as sound.

parts.explanation: Low-orbit satellites are much closer, so the signal delay is shorter.

explanation: Satellites use microwaves; digital signals can be regenerated without noise; low orbits are closer, so delays are shorter.
hints: Which waves pass through the atmosphere?
